sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: front versus rear no-zones, motorcycles versus mopeds, school buses on divided versus undivided roads, cyclist duties versus motorist duties, plus continuation facts on truck crashes, rider clues, cyclist safety, pedestrians and helping blind pedestrians
Confusable pairs among the sharing-the-road rules, followed by continuation facts that did not fit part C; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec09-R01 | anchor: A01
The handbook puts crashes between cars and commercial vehicles at more than 200,000 a year, many of them avoidable. [A01]
Why it matters: group trucks; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec09-R02 | anchor: A02
In the front no-zone the danger is cutting in too soon and slowing, which can get you rear-ended, while in the rear no-zone the danger is tailgating, where neither driver can see the other's situation. [A02]
Why it matters: group trucks; confusable front versus rear no-zone.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R03 | anchor: A02
Clues to a motorcyclist's next move include the rider or passenger turning their head to look back and the rider starting to lean or tilt the motorcycle. [A02]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R04 | anchor: A02
Strong winds or a rough road surface can push a motorcycle out of its position on the road. [A02]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec09-R05 | anchor: A03
Motorcycles need a license endorsement, while mopeds, limited in horsepower and to a top speed of 30 mph, must keep to the far right lane in most situations. [A03]
Why it matters: group two-wheelers; confusable motorcycle versus moped.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R06 | anchor: A03
On an undivided road, traffic in both directions stops for a school bus with flashing red lights, but on a divided highway only traffic going the same direction as the bus must stop. [A03]
Why it matters: group school buses; confusable divided versus undivided.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R07 | anchor: A03
Nevada lets school bus drivers report drivers who pass illegally to the school district and the DMV, and the vehicle's registered owner then receives a warning letter. [A03]
Why it matters: group school buses; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R08 | anchor: A03
Drivers around mopeds take the same precautions as around motorcycles, and moped riders share the same rights and duties as other drivers plus extra ones tied to their vehicle's limits. [A03]
Why it matters: group mopeds; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec09-R09 | anchor: A04
Cyclists must obey all signs and signals, and a cyclist who crosses an intersection in a crosswalk should get off and walk across as a pedestrian. [A04]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R10 | anchor: A04
A cyclist must give a hand signal once before turning unless in a designated turn lane or both hands are needed for safe control, and may signal a right turn with the right arm. [A04]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R11 | anchor: A04
Cyclists may not deliberately interfere with motor vehicles, just as motorists may not deliberately interfere with cyclists. [A04]
Why it matters: group bicycles; confusable cyclist versus motorist duties.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R12 | anchor: A04
Children and other inexperienced riders may not follow traffic rules, so give them extra care and expect the unexpected, and check both ways for cyclists when turning into an intersection or driveway. [A04]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R13 | anchor: A04
Cyclists should obey the law, wear a helmet and bright clothing and keep bikes repaired, and should not ride against traffic, wear headphones or earpieces, or ride at night without the required lights and reflectors. [A04]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec09-R14 | anchor: A05
Where there is a sidewalk pedestrians should use it, and where there is none they should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R15 | anchor: A05
A vehicle yielding to a pedestrian should wait until the person has crossed into the lanes heading the other way before moving on. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R16 | anchor: A05
Drive with extra care around pedestrians near schools, crosswalks, stop signs, signals and transit stops, especially when children are present. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R17 | anchor: A05
Pedestrians should use crosswalks and obey their signals, not start on a flashing Don't Walk, look left, right and left again, make eye contact with stopping drivers, and at night carry a flashlight and wear reflective gear. [A05]
Why it matters: group pedestrians; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec09-R18 | anchor: A06
Around a blind or visually impaired pedestrian, do not call out directions, do not honk, do not stop in the middle of the crosswalk and do not block the sidewalk. [A06]
Why it matters: group blind pedestrians; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec09-R19 | anchor: A06
Stop at every crosswalk where pedestrians are waiting, look before any right turn, and be extra alert for blind pedestrians when driving a nearly silent electric vehicle. [A06]
Why it matters: group blind pedestrians; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0067]
